verdict.justification: B is the stronger foundational workflow because it preserves the mandatory functional approvals while achieving agility through delegated authority, parallel approvals and delta-only pricing. Its explicit rule that every price change requires “Finance Controller, Program Manager and Purchase” directly matches the request, whereas A’s minor-change route merely keeps the “PM informed.” B also requires ER, Quality and Purchase sign-off on every TRSO revision; A permits ER and Quality to “acknowledge” minor changes without clearly establishing approval of the revised TRSO. Both provide useful modular quotation structures and actionable platform requirements, but B adds stronger implementation controls through quote reconciliation, cumulative-change tracking, explicit tooling thresholds and controlled ERP updates. B’s proceed-at-risk mechanism also specifies the required approval functions and a proposed true-up deadline, whereas A leaves provisional authorization less governed. Both drafts are overly dense for the requested 2–3-page executive document, particularly B, but B’s materially stronger governance and traceability outweigh its additional length.
